rounds.text: Amanta Healthcare Ltd is demonstrating exceptional market leadership and powerful momentum, sitting 91% of the way up its 52-week range and maintaining a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E42, E45]. Price action confirms structural strength, with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages while the 50-day average remains above the 200-day line [E44]. Fundamental cash generation is robust, underscored by an impressive cash conversion ratio of 3.20x for March 2026 where operating cash flow of Rs 48 Cr represents 93% of operating profit and proves that reported earnings are fully backed by hard cash [E28, E29, E31]. Furthermore, long-term profit growth has compounded at a healthy 22% over five years, supported by accelerating earnings dynamics and a supportive healthcare sector tailwind score of up to +0.90 [E17, E60, E66]. Domestic institutional confidence is clearly expanding, reflected by an increase in local institutional holdings to 12.92% in June 2026 from 11.34% in September 2025 [E37]. Conceded: [E39], [E40], [E41].

Amanta Healthcare Ltd trades at an inflated valuation that disconnects sharply from its underlying fundamentals, with a P/E ratio of 47.6x and a sector-adjusted P/E reaching 51.88x against a sector benchmark of 32.16x [E1, E6]. This premium pricing sits on top of deteriorating recent growth, demonstrated by a negative 4% TTM profit growth, a 3-year compounded sales growth of just 4%, and a negative margin of safety of -19.5% relative to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 157 per share [E15, E19, E39, E40]. Furthermore, the company exhibits mounting balance sheet strain with borrowings increasing to Rs 244 Cr and a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.11x, where debt exceeds net worth alongside a severe free cash flow burn of Rs -32 Cr in March 2026 [E30, E32, E33]. Compounding these risks, return profiles lag behind sector benchmarks significantly, with a low ROE of 7.46%, ROCE of 9.58%, and ROA of 2.63%, while institutional investors have registered a negative money flow with foreign holdings dropping by 0.57 percentage points [E8, E9, E10, E38]. Conceded: the company displays strong 5-year compounded profit growth of 22% and healthy operating cash flow of Rs 48 Cr that fully covers reported profit [E17, E28, E29, E53].

The bear targets valuation multiples like the 47.6x P/E [E1], but overlooks that the company's EV/EBITDA of 15.95x actually sits below the sector benchmark of 17.13x [E11]. While recent TTM profit growth dipped [E19], the bear ignores powerful medium-term earnings acceleration, specifically a phenomenal 114% compounded profit growth over 3 years and a solid 22% over 5 years [E18, E53]. Conceded: the DCF intrinsic value stands at Rs 157 against the current market price [E39], and free cash flow was negative at Rs -32 Cr [E30]; however, this coincides with a massive 1071.4% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 82 Cr [E34], proving cash is being actively reinvested into growth rather than wasted. On leverage concerns, the bear's focus on debt misses the vital operational reality that operating cash flow hit Rs 48 Cr in March 2026, delivering an exceptional 3.20x cash conversion where profits are fully backed by actual cash [E28, E29]. Finally, institutional outflows [E64] ignore the simultaneous expansion of domestic institutional holdings to 12.92% alongside an elite relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 backed by strong sector tailwinds [E37, E45, E67].

Conceded: EV/EBITDA of 15.95x sits below the sector benchmark of 17.13x [E11]. However, relying on this single enterprise multiple masks an inflated P/E of 47.6x and a premium 51.88x ratio against a sector benchmark of 32.16x, proving that the equity valuation is aggressively priced [E1, E6]. While the bull points to a 114% three-year profit growth [E18], this has violently reversed into a trailing-twelve-month contraction of -4% alongside a negative net profit trend of -6% YoY [E19, E63]. Conceded: capital work-in-progress surged by 1071.4% to Rs 82 Cr and operating cash flow hit Rs 48 Cr [E29, E34]; nevertheless, this aggressive growth spend has cratered free cash flow to negative Rs -32 Cr while driving total borrowings up to Rs 244 Cr and pushing debt-to-equity to 1.11x, meaning debt now exceeds net worth [E30, E32, E33]. Furthermore, pointing to domestic institutional accumulation ignores the broader institutional outflow and a net negative institutional money flow reading of -0.38 percentage points [E37, E38, E64]. Finally, the elite relative-strength rating of 100 cannot obscure a dangerous price-led disconnect where recent price growth outpaces profit growth by 45%, leaving expectations running far ahead of delivery [E45, E51].
